title: Check Before You Dilate

patient.name: Mdm Tham Yoke Lan
patient.presenting_complaint: Sent for dilation before a fundus check, but mentions she once had a sudden very painful red eye that was treated as 'narrow angle'

history.hpc: Mdm Tham is sent for pupil dilation. While preparing her, she mentions: 'Last time my eye suddenly very pain and red, doctor say my angle narrow, must be careful with dilating drops.' This history of a narrow drainage angle / previous acute angle-closure is a contraindication to routine dilation that must be checked with the nurse/doctor first.
history.pmhx: Previous acute angle-closure episode (narrow angles). Hypertension.
medications: possibly prior laser iridotomy — to confirm
history.social_hx: Lives with husband. Came for routine review.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: History of narrow angles; shallow anterior chamber possible — do not dilate before clarifying
examination_findings.fundus: Pending decision on whether/how to dilate

investigations.front_line_action: Recognise the history of narrow angles / previous acute angle-closure as a contraindication to routine dilation. Do NOT instil dilating drops. Check with the nurse/doctor before dilating — they may confirm a prior laser iridotomy or choose a safer approach (or a procedure that does not need dilation).
investigations.documentation: Record the narrow-angle history and that dilation was held pending doctor/nurse confirmation.

diagnosis: A relative contraindication to routine pupil dilation: a history of narrow angles / previous acute angle-closure, where dilating drops could precipitate an angle-closure attack. The PSA competency is eliciting and recognising this history, withholding dilation, and checking with the nurse/doctor before proceeding.

immediate: Before dilating, ask about and recognise the narrow-angle / previous acute glaucoma history as a contraindication
Do NOT instil dilating drops until cleared
Check with the nurse/doctor before dilating (they may confirm a prior iridotomy or choose a safer option)
Document the history and that dilation was held pending confirmation
Keep the patient informed and reassured while you check
Proceed only as directed by the nurse/doctor
follow_up: Doctor/nurse to decide whether dilation is safe (e.g., post-iridotomy) or to use an alternative
If dilated after clearance, give standard post-dilation advice and watch for symptoms of angle closure
Record the decision and any instructions
patient_education: Thank her for telling you about the narrow-angle history — explain it is important
Explain you need to check with the doctor/nurse before using dilating drops for safety
If cleared and dilated, advise her to report any sudden pain, redness, or haloes immediately
Reassure her this caution is to protect her eye

key_points: Asks about previous acute red/painful eye and narrow-angle history before dilating
Recognises the significance of the previous acute angle-closure episode
Checks for prior treatment (e.g., laser iridotomy)
Confirms the indication for the planned dilation
Identifies the narrow-angle history as a contraindication to routine dilation
Checks with the nurse/doctor before proceeding
Documents the history and the held dilation
Understands dilation can precipitate angle closure in narrow angles
Recognises this as a contraindication needing clearance
Knows a prior iridotomy may change the decision
Knows the decision to dilate rests with the doctor/nurse
Does not dilate before checking with the nurse/doctor
Documents the contraindication and the action taken
Keeps the patient informed and reassured
Gives appropriate warning advice if later dilated
